headlines.article_text: Oil earnings Chevron (CVX) and Exxon (XOM) Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu In this article CVX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The Chevron logo is seen alongside diesel prices above $7 a gallon at a truck stop in Commerce, California on August 26, 2026. Patrick T. Fallon | Afp | Getty Images Chevron and Exxon Mobil on Friday reported profits that surged in the third quarter, as their U.S. refineries ran at full capacity to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices. Chevron's net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 a share, compared to $3.5 billion, or $1.82 a share, in the same period last year. When adjusted for one-time items, it reported earnings of $5.28 per share, soundly beating Wall Street's expectations of $4.89. Diesel prices have surged globally as Ukraine and Iran have bombed refineries in Russia and the Middle East. U.S. refiners have ramped up production to fill the supply gap. Exxon Mobil's profits doubled to $15.4 billion, or $3.72 a share, compared to $7.5 billion, or $1.76 a share, in the same period in 2025. When adjusted for one-time items, it posted earnings of $4.23 a share, beating the Street's expectations. Chevron shares are up about 2% in premarket trading, while Exxon is trading about 1.5% higher. Here's how Chevron and Exxon did, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Chevron's earnings per share: $5.28 adjusted, vs. $4.89 expected Chevron's revenue: $67.8 billion, vs. $61.6 billion expected Exxon's earnings per share: $4.23 adjusted, vs. $4.08 expected Exxon's revenue: $113.2 billion, vs. $103.1 billion expected Chevron's U.S. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. Diesel and jet fuel yields rose more than 10%, the company said. Exxon said its Gulf Coast refineries operated at 100% utilization with the second-high diesel production on record at those facilities. Profits from Chevron's refining division surged more than 300% to $4.9 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Profits from Chevron's oil and gas production rose about 70% to $5.7 billion compared to $3.3 billion in the year-ago period. Its output actually declined slightly to 3.9 million bpd compared to about 4 million bpd in the same period last year. The decline was in its international segment due in part to the conflict in the Middle East, while output was largely flat in the U.S. year over year. headlines.article_text: BP’s third-quarter profit nearly quadruples as refining margins surge Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points BP’s underlying profit nearly quadrupled year on year to $8.5 billion in the third quarter, beating analyst expectations of $6.19 billion. The company cited stronger gas and marketing trading and significantly higher refining margins. Refining margins surged as supply disruptions tightened fuel markets, but CEO Meg O’Neill said BP expects some easing in the fourth quarter. BP is strengthening its balance sheet to support shareholder returns through the cycle. Operating cash flow rose to $28.55 billion in the first nine months, from $16.89 billion a year earlier, while net debt fell to $13.87 billion. O’Neill said the company is also setting aside extra cash for its remaining obligations over the Deepwater Horizon disaster. In this article BP Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 7:56 07:56 BP CEO: The macro environment is a tailwind Squawk Box Europe Oil major BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple year-on-year. The company reported $8.5 billion in underlying replacement cost profit, used as a proxy for net profit. That was above the $6.191 billion forecast by analysts in an LSEG-compiled consensus and up from $2.2 billion a year ago . Operating cash flow hit $28.55 billion across the first nine months of the year, up from $16.89 billion in 2025, while net debt fell to $13.87 billion from $26.05 billion across the same period. The result primarily reflects better performance in gas and marketing trading, and "significantly higher" realized refining margins, BP said. "These are dynamic times with volatility and disruption to trade flows continuing to define energy markets," BP CEO Meg O'Neill said in a statement. "The industry as a whole has been showing remarkable adaptability. Refineries have been running close to capacity to make up for shortfalls, shipping has been taking different and longer routes, and releases from strategic and commercial reserves are helping to bridge supply gap." Demand outlook Rivals Shell and TotalEnergies on Thursday said their refining margins — the amount earned from processing crude oil into products like diesel, jet fuel and gasoline — hit historically high levels . Outages and damage to refineries from global conflicts, from the Russia-Ukraine war to the Middle East, have created tightness in global fuel markets this year, pushing product prices sharply higher relative to crude . Benchmark crude prices have also been hugely volatile this year as traders reacted swiftly to unpredictable newsflow coming from the U.S. and Israel's war with Iran, and remain nearly double their level a year ago. ICE Brent crude price. Analysts have been questioning when and if high energy prices will ultimately drive demand destruction, easing pressures on constrained refineries, as the premium for refined products over crude remains at decade-highs. BP CEO O'Neill told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday that BP's refining indicator margin for the quarter of $46.7 a barrel was "incredibly strong" and "indicative of demand for the products we produce," boosted by refining reliability of over 96%. "We've been able to adapt and try to adjust our refining runs to meet... the needs for the product that is most in demand," she said. "Now, if we roll forward, we are seeing refining margins start to soften a bit ... third quarter is always a big driving period and a big holiday period. So, fourth quarter demand typically drops off. That is bringing the refining margins down a bit." "But again, what we control is our ability to run our facilities safely and reliably to try to capture the opportunity that presents itself." BP announced a new strategy last year that sees the energy giant pivot back towards its traditional oil and gas operations and away from renewables. It also announced a consolidation of its leadership structure and debt reduction. O'Neill told CNBC on Friday that BP was focused on strengthening its balance sheet to give shareholders "confidence that they can be rewarded through the cycle." "So, oil prices today are strong. They will not always be strong. I've got 30 years in the industry, and the prices go up and down. And at some point, they will fall again. So we need to design a company and a financial frame and a balance sheet that allows us to reward shareholders through the cycle." That includes addressing its financial obligations, including the $5.9 billion it still owes the U.S. government and states for settlements over the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010 , which it intends to ringfence extra cash for, she said. "Deepwater Horizon was an incredible tragedy, and it has shaped BP. We will not forget the 11 men who lost their lives, or the impact that we had on the Gulf Coast and the environment there," she said. "So we have deeply embedded those lessons, but we're in a position now where we want to take care of those financial obligations going forward to ensure we're a more resilient company in future years."
